TGO.note: Authentication and verification mechanisms are described as a future need, not as under way or in service.
Communes' civil status role is mentioned, but no exchange of records between civil register and ID system is stated.

facts.fact: ANID reports more than six million people registered in the e-ID Togo national identification register as of 28 September 2026, about 70% of the 8.6 million population (share computed from the held population).
The same figure of more than six million people registered is about 70% of the held population of 8.6 million, above two-thirds (share computed from the held population).

TGO.note: Each registered person gets a unique number, but at enrolment, not at birth; new generations are to be integrated progressively.

facts.fact: The national identification agency ANID's teams carried out biometric registration across the regions to build the national identification register.
Togo chose MOSIP, an open-source identity platform, to build the infrastructure, which the article says lets the country keep control of it.

TGO.note: No public register keyed on the national ID number is stated.

facts.fact: ANID has produced about 5.9 million identification cards, nearly 80% reportedly distributed, and each person registered receives a Unique Identification Number (NIU), per data reported on 28 September 2026.
